UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores core information about a user or a specialist within the NutriPath AI application, including their personal details and role.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

email.description: The user's email address, used for login and communication.

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

profileType.description: Indicates whether the user is a 'RegularUser' or a 'Specialist'.

dateJoined.description: The timestamp when the user registered their profile.

HealthDataInput.title: HealthDataInput
HealthDataInput.description: Records a user's essential health metrics and personal goals at a specific point in time, serving as primary input for AI recommendations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HealthDataInput entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile this health data belongs to. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N HealthDataInput)

weightKg.description: The user's current weight in kilograms.

heightCm.description: The user's current height in centimeters.

ageYears.description: The user's current age in years.

activityLevel.description: The user's self-reported physical activity level.

submissionDate.description: The timestamp when this specific health data record was submitted.

DietaryLog.title: DietaryLog
DietaryLog.description: Stores optional, free-form text input from a user detailing their daily food intake for AI analysis.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DietaryLog entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile this dietary log belongs to. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N DietaryLog)

logDate.description: The timestamp when this dietary log entry was created or pertains to.

foodIntakeText.description: Free-form text provided by the user describing their food intake.

LabResult.title: LabResult
LabResult.description: Stores optional, free-form text input from a user regarding their recent lab analysis results for AI consideration.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LabResult entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile this lab result belongs to. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N LabResult)

resultDate.description: The timestamp when these lab results were submitted or pertain to.

labResultText.description: Free-form text containing the user's lab analysis results.

Recommendation.title: Recommendation
Recommendation.description: Stores the AI-generated personalized health recommendations for a user, based on their provided data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Recommendation entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile for whom this recommendation was generated. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Recommendation)

healthDataInputId.description: Reference to the specific HealthDataInput that was used as the primary basis for this recommendation. (Relationship: HealthDataInput 1:N Recommendation)

generationDate.description: The timestamp when this recommendation was generated by the AI.

lifestyleRecommendations.description: AI-generated recommendations regarding lifestyle adjustments, such as exercise and sleep.

dietaryRecommendations.description: AI-generated recommendations regarding diet plans and food choices.

supplementRecommendations.description: AI-generated recommendations regarding suitable vitamin and supplement intake.

relevantDietaryLogIds.description: References to DietaryLog entries that were considered by the AI when generating this recommendation. (Relationship: DietaryLog N:N Recommendation)

relevantLabResultIds.description: References to LabResult entries that were considered by the AI when generating this recommendation. (Relationship: LabResult N:N Recommendation)

definition.description: Stores core information about a user or specialist. The document ID `{userId}` must match `UserProfile.id` and `request.auth.uid`. Authorization is self-owned.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, corresponding to `request.auth.uid`.

definition.description: Records a user's health metrics and goals. Owned by the user specified in the path. Authorization relies on `userId` in the path matching `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this health data input.

params.name: healthDataInputId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific health data input record.

definition.description: Stores a user's free-form dietary log entries. Owned by the user specified in the path. Authorization relies on `userId` in the path matching `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this dietary log.

params.name: dietaryLogId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific dietary log entry.

definition.description: Stores a user's free-form lab analysis results. Owned by the user specified in the path. Authorization relies on `userId` in the path matching `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this lab result.

params.name: labResultId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific lab result entry.

definition.description: Stores AI-generated health recommendations for a user. Owned by the user specified in the path. Authorization relies on `userId` in the path matching `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user for whom this recommendation was generated.

params.name: recommendationId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific recommendation.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following a strict hierarchical, user-centric model, prioritizing Authorization Independence and secure List operations (QAPs). 

1.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** UserProfile documents are stored in the top-level `users` collection. The document ID (`{userId}`) for each UserProfile directly corresponds to the authenticated user's UID (`request.auth.uid`). This establishes clear, path-based ownership for each user's root profile data.

2.  **User-Specific Subcollections:** All other entities (`HealthDataInput`, `DietaryLog`, `LabResult`, `Recommendation`) are stored as subcollections under the respective user's profile: `/users/{userId}/<subcollectionName>/{docId}`.

    *   `/users/{userId}/healthDataInputs/{healthDataInputId}`
    *   `/users/{userId}/dietaryLogs/{dietaryLogId}`
    *   `/users/{userId}/labResults/{labResultId}`
    *   `/users/{userId}/recommendations/{recommendationId}`

**Authorization Independence:** This design achieves Authorization Independence by incorporating the `userId` directly into the path of every user-owned document. For example, to access a `HealthDataInput`, the security rule can directly compare `request.auth.uid` with the `{userId}` wildcard in the path (`/users/{userId}/healthDataInputs/{healthDataInputId}`). This eliminates the need for `get()` calls to parent documents (e.g., `UserProfile` or other subcollection documents) to verify ownership or relationships, making security rules atomic, simpler, and more performant. Each document inherently carries its authorization context through its path.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This structure inherently supports secure `list` operations. Because all user-specific data resides under `/users/{userId}/...`, any `list` query initiated by an authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`) on their own subcollections (e.g., `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('healthDataInputs').get()`) will automatically be restricted by rules like `allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. The Firestore security rules enforce that the `userId` wildcard in the path must match `request.auth.uid`, guaranteeing that `list` operations only return documents owned by the authenticated user. This prevents rules from acting as filters and ensures all returned data is explicitly authorized. The `profileType` field within `UserProfile` allows for role-based access control to the user's *own* profile, but no cross-user access is enabled by default with this structure, aligning with the principle of homogeneous security posture per collection.
